head: 0eda551660b532402cae81be88cedc9e32d72165
target: Apple Silicon Macs, initially 24 GiB RAM

findings.title: No oMLX installation or MLX model support
findings.evidence: Installer and catalog exclusively manage llama.cpp/GGUF. Actual --check on this 24 GiB Mac recommends Qwen3.6 35B Q3 and llama.cpp b11146.

findings.title: Failed Pi smoke test still returns success
findings.evidence: Fresh HOME with private Node/Pi and artificial GGUF bootstraps successfully. A deliberately insufficient 2048 context causes the real Pi request to fail; installer prints a warning followed by success/exit 0. Re-run with 8192 also fails to produce meaningful tiny-model output and remains successful. Tiny random weights test transport only, never quality.

findings.title: Disabled required provider is not repaired or rejected
findings.evidence: Applying the real settings merge to a fixture with extensions=[-builtin:llama.cpp] leaves it disabled, while setting defaultProvider=llama.cpp. Real Pi invocation then exits 1: Unknown provider llama.cpp. This also matches the live Mac preference after old-router cleanup.

findings.title: Best model means static rank under estimated memory budget
findings.evidence: Model recommendation sorts by fixed rank and estimates fit. It performs no quality comparison, responsiveness test, peak-memory qualification or runtime fallback after an out-of-memory load failure.

findings.title: Pi and addon versions are not reproducible
findings.evidence: Pi and default addons use unversioned npm specs; Node uses latest-v24.x; compatible external Pi >=1.0.0 is reused. llama.cpp and model weights are pinned, but the whole stack is not.

findings.title: Doctor reports intentionally omitted addons as missing
findings.evidence: Clean install with documented --no-packages succeeds, but doctor exits 1 with five missing-addon problems. Preference is not recorded for doctor/update.

findings.title: Rollback covers legacy server migration, not full install transaction
findings.evidence: Legacy rollback guard ends after server validation; Pi install/configuration/package/smoke stages happen afterward. Current managed server replacement also does not retain an end-to-end validated previous model selection.

proposedContract.platformGate: Native Apple Silicon, supported macOS, RAM and free disk checks before install
proposedContract.profiles: Curated tested tuples of engine, model revision, tokenizer/template, context, reasoning and sampling; default chosen by quality then practical latency within memory budget
proposedContract.omlx: Versioned official macOS app runtime with precompiled kernels, isolated managed loopback service; compatible existing install may be reused explicitly
proposedContract.models: MLX snapshot file manifest with hashes; optional llama.cpp backend for GGUF models such as currently installed Saluki
proposedContract.install: Staged downloads, checksum verification, atomic activation, preserve existing Pi providers and unrelated settings
proposedContract.validation: Real Pi answer, real tool round trip on fixture, cold restart and no duplicate server, context budget, per-model memory/latency smoke threshold
proposedContract.maintenance: Idempotent repair, doctor checks actual provider/model request, rollback complete stack; updates offer tested profiles rather than silently selecting newest/largest
proposedContract.scope: No Windows/Linux work required for first release
proposedContract.selectionPolicy: Do not download and benchmark every candidate during installation. Ship a versioned, task-tested recommended profile plus an explicit fast/quality alternative. RAM fit alone cannot establish the best model, and 24 GiB Macs differ in compute and memory bandwidth.
proposedContract.currentInstalledStackIsNotPortable: Qwen autostart currently imports Pippa server helpers and Saluki uses /Applications/Pippa.app/Contents/Helpers/llama-server. A standalone pi-local-agent installer must own or explicitly reuse these dependencies; copying current models.json to a fresh Mac is insufficient.
proposedContract.newMachineClaim: A fake clean HOME validates bootstrap and configuration isolation on this Mac, not a clean OS image, login launchd integration, other M-series chips or macOS 15.
